synopsis: AutoMIP contributes a method for coupling persistent research hypotheses with compatible executable states and evaluator feedback. Its evidentiary role for pieces 02 and 03 is a developer-reported computational benchmark study and a practical example of experiment bookkeeping, rather than independent validation. The selected passages support discussion of delegated experiment selection and execution, verification requirements, ablations, resource budgets, failures and reporting discrepancies. The supplied September 30 publication date falls within the authoritative September 16–October 15 window. This card extracts the supplied source only; later substantive claims must cite its exact passages.
limitations_and_counterevidence: The supplied material contains no independent replication or external researcher assessment. Benchmark success does not establish general research autonomy, and per-instance outcome/time/token tables do not provide objective values or independently checked solution certificates. Several protocol subsections contain only headings, and Appendix B explicitly supplies standardized templates rather than historical prompts. Cost reporting requires reconciliation: Metrics defines tokens as averages including unsuccessful runs, while the ablation discussion calls its figure a total; no monetary cost is supplied. Table 4 reports 41,089 seconds for AutoMIP’s single 6–12-hour success, whereas Appendix H records the late acopf_caseactivsg70k_qcqp success at 24,199 seconds. These passages preserve the discrepancy without resolving it. The Open-set stockholm row shows a baseline success where AutoMIP reports failure. Other agent interfaces failed to complete evaluations in the tested configurations. These are orientation notes, not substitutes for passage citations.

passages.purpose: Method and evidentiary role: the authors describe hypothesis management, compatible-state restoration and evaluation feedback; this is a proposed workflow, not proof that every verification was correct.

locator.quote: AutoMIP couples a persistent idea pool with an algorithm tree to jointly manage research hypotheses and executable experimental states. A review-and-ideation layer generates and maintains diverse research directions from accumulated evidence; an algorithm-search layer selects refinements or switches between directions while restoring compatible historical states and artifacts; and a verification layer executes candidates, validates their outcomes, and feeds the resulting evidence back into the exploration process.

passages.purpose: Experimental scope and resource budget: distinguish incumbent improvement, fixed-target attainment and nonlinear tasks; preserve the stated hardware and model configurations.

locator.quote:
We first assess AutoMIP in MIPLib. Open and Hard set each comprises 60 instances ([Gleixner et al., 2021](#bib.bib10)). For Open set, we seek a strict improvement over the best known solution,
or first feasibility when no feasible solution is found yet, within 43,200 s. For Hard set, we seek a specified historical objective target within 3,600 s. We also use a 60-instance MINLPLib cohort with a 43,200 s horizon. Given these different tasks, we assess AutoMIP in terms of incumbent improvement, fixed-target attainment, and nonlinear optimization, respectively.
All configurations run on an Apple M4 Pro machine with 12 logical CPUs, 12 physical CPU cores, and 24 GB memory. Codex-based configurations use GPT-5.5, whereas the Claude Code interface uses Claude Sonnet 5.

passages.purpose: Ablation methods and reported results: supports a bounded comparison on 20 Open instances, including the authors’ interpretation of complementary benefits.

locator.quote:
NoPool removes the idea pool while retaining algorithm tree, generating a new research direction only when a direction switch is triggered. NoTree retains the idea pool and its random selection of unused research directions, but replaces the algorithm tree with a linear execution history, preventing experimental state reuse. Appendix [A.6](#A1.SS6) details the retained and removed components.
As shown in Table [3](#S4.T3), on 20 Open-set instances, AutoMIP successfully completes 15 tasks (75.0%), compared with 12 (60.0%) for NoPool and 10 (50.0%) for NoTree. It also achieves the best final objective on 9 instances, versus 4 for NoPool and 2 for NoTree. The degradation of both ablations indicates that the idea pool and algorithm tree provide complementary benefits: the former preserves diverse research directions, while the latter enables effective reuse of compatible experimental states.

passages.purpose: Cost denominator: retain the explicit average-token definition and inclusion of unsuccessful runs; read alongside the conflicting total-token wording.

locator.quote: Token values represent average token consumption over all instances (in each time interval), including unsuccessful runs.

passages.purpose: Reported cost comparison and internal inconsistency: the ablation discussion calls these figures totals, unlike the Metrics definition. Do not convert this into a verified total budget or monetary saving.

locator.quote: It also uses the fewest tokens overall, with 1,070,460 total tokens, compared with 1,558,655 for NoPool and 1,683,805 for NoTree, representing reductions of 31.3% and 36.4%, respectively.

passages.purpose: MINLPLib comparison and timing discrepancy, first side: Table 4 reports AutoMIP 52 successes versus Codex 45, with one AutoMIP success in the 6–12-hour interval at 41,089 seconds. Preserve headings to distinguish wins, successes, time and tokens.

Timing discrepancy, second side: Appendix H records the late nonlinear success at 24,199 seconds. Columns are AutoMIP, Codex and Loop, each with result, time and token fields; reconcile with Table 4 before using timing headlines.

Counterevidence to universal superiority: Appendix D records AutoMIP failure on stockholm while Codex and Loop succeed. Columns are AutoMIP, Codex and Loop, each with result, time and token fields; retain the unusual populated fields after AutoMIP’s NO label unchanged.
Reproducibility qualification: Appendix B distinguishes reusable prompt templates from the historical prompts actually used.

locator.quote: These reusable English templates specify the Open and Hard objectives and stopping rules. Replace {METHOD} with PoolTree, AutoEoH, Loop, or EvoX, and fill the instance, skill path, run directory, and objective. For plain Codex, omit the exploration-skill reading instruction and access permission; retain the same task, budget, verification, and isolation rules. These are standardized templates, not verbatim historical prompts.

passages.purpose: Operational limitation and incomplete comparison: other tested interfaces did not sustain the required runs; this supports a configuration-specific failure report, not a general ranking of those systems.

locator.quote: We also attempted to run AutoMIP in DeepSeek Harness ([DeepSeek-AI, 2026](#bib.bib20)), Gemini CLI ([Google, 2025](#bib.bib22)), and DeerFlow ([ByteDance, 2025](#bib.bib21)). In our tested configurations, these systems could not sustain the required twelve-hour runs, so these attempts did not yield completed evaluations and are not included in Table [5](#S4.T5).
